We have mass spec: m/z 180.0423 (intensity 100) etc. Likely molecular ion at 180.0423. That suggests formula C10H12NO2? Let's calculate exact mass: C10H13NO2 = 179.099? Actually compute: C10 = 120.000, H13 = 13.101, N = 14.003, O2 = 31.989 => total 179.093. Not 180.042. Let's compute C10H12NO2: H12 = 12.094, total 120+12.094+14.003+31.989=178.086. Not 180.042. Maybe includes Na? But m/z 180.042 likely corresponds to C9H10NO3? Let's compute: C9=108, H10=10.079, N=14.003, O3=47.985 => total 180.067. Slightly higher. C9H9NO3? H9=9.07 => total 179.058. Not. C10H12N2O? C10=120, H12=12.094, N2=28.006, O=15.995 => 176.095. Not.

Let's compute exact mass of C10H13NO2: using monoisotopic: C 12.0000, H 1.007825, N 14.003074, O 15.994915. So mass = 10*12 =120 +13*1.007825=13.101725 +14.003074 +2*15.994915=31.98983 => total 179.094629. Not 180.042.

What about C10H12NO3? mass =120 +12.0939 +14.003074 +3*15.994915=47.984745 => total 194.081? Wait compute: 120+12.0939=132.0939; +14.003074=146.096974; +47.984745=194.081719. Too high.

C9H10NO2? mass =108 +10.07825 +14.003074 +31.98983 =164.071? Actually 108+10.078=118.078; +14.003=132.081; +31.989=164.07.

C9H12NO3? 108+12.094=120.094; +14.003=134.097; +47.985=182.082. Slightly higher than 180.042.

C8H10N2O2? 96+10.078=106.078; +28.006=134.084; +31.989=166.073.

Maybe the ion is [M+H]+? If m/z 180.042 corresponds to M+H, then neutral mass =179.034. That matches C10H13NO2 (179.094) not close. Let's compute exact mass of C9H10NO3 (180.067). M+H would be 181.074. Not.

What about C9H8NO3? mass =108+8.0626+14.003+47.985=178.051. M+H 179.058.

Our observed m/z 180.042 maybe corresponds to C9H8N2O2? mass =108+8.0626+28.006+31.989=176.058. Not.

Let's compute formula from mass using typical: 180.042 - maybe C10H8O3? mass =120+8.0626+3*15.9949=120+8.0626+47.985=176.0476. Not.

C11H12O2? mass =132+12.094+31.989=176.083.

C11H12N? mass =132+12.094+14.003=158.097.

C9H12O3? mass =108+12.094+47.985=168.079.

C8H8N2O3? 96+8.0626+28.006+47.985=180.054. That's close! C8H8N2O3 exact mass: 96 + 8.0626 =104.0626; +28.006=132.0686; +47.985=180.0536. Observed 180.042, diff 0.0116.

C7H6N2O4? 84+6.047=90.047; +28.006=118.053; +63.979=182.032.

Maybe the ion is [M+Na]+? Na 22.9898, so neutral mass =157.052. That could be C9H10NO2 (164.07) not.

Let's look at carbon NMR: peaks at 170.20, 169.60 (likely carbonyl carbons, maybe carboxylic acid and amide). 151.28 (aromatic C attached to hetero). 134.64, 132.51, 124.01, 123.09, 122.26 (aromatic carbons). 20.67 (alkyl methyl). So aromatic ring with two carbonyls (maybe amide and carboxylic acid). Methyl attached to carbonyl (acetyl). So structure could be acetanilide with carboxylic acid substituent? That's p-aminobenzoic acid acetylated? Actually acetanilide is C8H9NO, carbonyl at 170? but only one carbonyl. Here we have two carbonyls ~170 each, suggests amide carbonyl and carboxylic acid carbonyl. Aromatic ring with substituents: maybe para-aminobenzoic acid acetylated (acetanilide with carboxylic acid). That would be N-acetyl-p-aminobenzoic acid (also known as acetanilide-4-carboxylic acid). SMILES: CC(=O)Nc1ccc(C(=O)O)cc1. That's what we attempted earlier. Let's compute formula: C9? Actually count: CC(=O)N = C2H3NO? Wait: CC(=O)N = C2H3NO? Actually CH3-CO-N: C2 H3? CH3 (C1 H3) + CO (C1 O1) + N (N1) => C2 H3 N1 O1? plus aromatic ring C6 H4 (since two substituents replace two H). plus carboxylic acid C(=O)O adds C1 O2 H1? Actually COOH adds C1 O2 H1. So total C2+6+1 =9 carbons? Wait we have CC(=O)N attached to ring, plus COOH attached to ring. So total C = 2 (acetyl) +6 (ring) +1 (carboxyl) =9. H: CH3 gives 3, amide N has H? In SMILES N attached to carbonyl and aromatic, so N-H present: 1 H. Aromatic ring hydrogens: 4 (since two substituents). Carboxylic OH: 1 H. Total H =3+1+4+1=9. N=1, O: carbonyl of acetyl O1, carbonyl of acid O1, OH O1 =3 O. So formula C9H9NO3? Wait we have 9 H? Let's recount: CH3 (3), N-H (1), aromatic H (4), COOH OH (1) =9. So C9H9NO3. But mass of C9H9NO3 = 179.058? compute: 108 +9.0704 +14.003 +47.985 =179.058. M+H =180.065. Observed 180.042, close but 0.023 diff. Could be measurement error.

Carbon NMR: carbonyls at 170.2 and 169.6 matches amide and acid. Aromatic carbons around 151 (maybe ipso attached to N), 134,132,124,123,122 typical. Methyl carbon at 20.7 matches acetyl methyl. So structure fits.

Thus SMILES: CC(=O)Nc1ccc(C(=O)O)cc1

We validated SMILES is valid. Need to ensure formula matches mass. Let's compute exact mass of C9H9NO3: using monoisotopic: C9 108, H9 9.070425, N 14.003074, O3 47.984745 =179.058244. M+H =180.066069. Observed 180.042, diff 0.024. Could be [M+Na]+? M+Na would be 202.04. Not.

Maybe the ion observed is [M+H]+ of C9H8NO3? That mass 178.051, not.

But carbon NMR shows methyl, so must have CH3. So C9H9NO3 plausible.

Thus answer SMILES.

We should maybe double-check with simulate spectra to confirm? Could be expensive but okay. Let's simulate to see if matches carbon NMR peaks.
